module.dkim.checks: Queries about a hundred common DKIM selectors, then analyses every key found: type, RSA size, test mode, hash, provider delegation. Tells revoked keys and DNS wildcards apart.
module.dkim.fix:
Find each key in the result (selector, type, size) and the service that signs with it (mail platform, newsletter, CRM). Delete the `selector._domainkey` records of services you no longer use from DNS.
RSA key of 1024 bits or less: generate a 2048-bit key from the sending service (the DKIM page of its admin console) or with OpenSSL if you run the server, publish it under a NEW selector, then switch signing to that selector. If your DNS console limits a text value to 255 characters, split the key into several quoted strings: they are joined end to end.
Selector that is a CNAME to the provider (Microsoft 365, for example): the key belongs to the provider; start or request the rotation to 2048 bits from its admin console instead of editing DNS.
Once messages are signed with the new selector (`DKIM-Signature` header, `s=` field), wait a few days and then delete the old record: the rotation causes no interruption.
Key in test mode (`t=y`): remove `t=y` from the record once signing is validated; while it is present, recipients do not enforce DKIM.
Key limited to SHA-1 (`h=sha1`): remove the `h=` tag (or set it to `h=sha256`) and check that the service signs with `rsa-sha256`; SHA-1 is prohibited for DKIM (RFC 8301).
Unreadable key: copy the exact value the service gives you, with no space, line break or typographic quote; only a deliberately revoked key has an empty `p=`.
Check with `dig +short TXT selector._domainkey.example.com`, send a message to an external mailbox and confirm `dkim=pass` in the `Authentication-Results` header. Plan a rotation at least once a year.
module.dkim.fix_snippet:
# DNS
selector2026._domainkey.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=PUBLIC_KEY_FROM_YOUR_SENDING_SERVICE"
# OpenSSL
openssl genrsa -out dkim-selector2026.key 2048
openssl rsa -in dkim-selector2026.key -pubout -outform der | openssl base64 -A
# dig
dig +short TXT selector2026._domainkey.example.com
module.dkim.title: DKIM keys
module.dkim.why: DKIM proves a message was not altered and really comes from the domain. A short key can be broken, and a key in test mode is not enforced by receivers.
